name: Group 42 Holding Ltd (G42)
employees: Group total not disclosed; Core42 cites '1100+ AI & Cloud Experts' and Khazna's NexOps unit 230+ operations staff

ownership.notes: Chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's National Security Adviser, who also chairs MGX. G42's own site names its investors as 'Mubadala, SilverLake, Microsoft, and the Dalio Family Office', with no percentages. Microsoft invested US$1.5B for a minority stake in April 2024, and Brad Smith joined the board. Two subsidiaries are listed on ADX: Presight and Space42. Khazna Data Center Holdings Limited is majority-owned by G42; MGX and Silver Lake became minority shareholders in March 2025, when e& sold its 40% for US$2.2B (AED 8.0B), and their percentages are undisclosed. Bloomberg reports exploratory talks on selling a majority stake to US companies or creating a US-based vehicle (4 Sep 2026) and on raising 'billions of dollars' (2 Sep 2026); no decision is reported.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: G42 is Abu Dhabi's state-aligned AI group, and through Khazna Data Centers it owns the UAE's dominant data-centre landlord. Khazna 'designs, builds and operates' 30 live data centres totalling almost 650 MW, holds a 73% share of the UAE market and is developing more than 1 GW more. It is building the 1 GW Stargate UAE cluster for OpenAI and Oracle inside the 5 GW UAE–US AI Campus. The first 200 MW is targeted for 2026, and G42 said in October 2025 the project had 'completed procurement of all long-lead equipment'. No supplier, and no signing entity, is named. Core42, its neocloud arm, sells sovereign AI cloud and is a 60 MW tenant at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus. On 10 Jul 2026 the US moved the UAE to Country Group A:5 and named G42 and Core42 licence-free recipients of advanced chips — an approval that 'shall automatically expire on April 6, 2027' unless they become US companies. The only named power-architecture link is a Khazna–Siemens memorandum (15 Sep 2026): 'The companies will continue to progress next-generation 800 VDC power architectures' — a memorandum, not an award. BACKGROUND: Founded in 2018, chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, run by Group CEO Peng Xiao. Microsoft invested US$1.5B in 2024 under an Intergovernmental Assurance Agreement and runs Azure in the UAE through Core42's sovereign cloud; Khazna is delivering a 200 MW Azure expansion from the end of 2026. G42 publishes no group financials. Khazna's implied equity value at e&'s exit was about US$5.5B, and it carries a US$2.62B, up-to-10-year facility from ADCB and FAB. Reuters (11 Sep 2026) reports the 5 GW campus will likely be spread across the UAE after the Iranian strikes on Gulf data centres. The FT reported in 2025 US intelligence findings that G42 technology reached Huawei, which G42 calls 'false and defamatory'.
ecosystemRole: We assess G42 as the corpus's first Gulf landlord-and-neocloud group, and — through Khazna — the named builder and most likely equipment buyer for Stargate UAE, OpenAI's first 'OpenAI for Countries' campus. Basis: e&'s ADX filing says 'Khazna designs, builds and operates wholesale data centers'. G42's construction update says Stargate UAE is 'being developed by Khazna Data Centers' on a 'design-to-build approach' and that 'the project has completed procurement of all long-lead equipment'. Khazna carries its own debt, buys its own land and appoints its own general contractors (Laing O'Rourke on earlier sites). Core42, by contrast, leases shells and buys IT. For a power-equipment seller the door is Khazna's engineering organisation, the one G42 entity with an 800 VDC conversation on the record (Siemens memorandum, September 2026). The constraint is US export policy: the group's chip access sunsets on 6 Apr 2027 unless it restructures as a US company.

productsAndServices.name: Khazna Data Centers — wholesale and hyperscale campuses
productsAndServices.description: Khazna is G42's data-centre landlord: 'Khazna designs, builds and operates wholesale data centers' (e& ADX filing). It runs '30 live data centers, representing a portfolio of almost 650MW' (Dec 2025), claims a 73% share of the UAE market, and is 'delivering over 1GW of additional AI-ready capacity across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Italy and other key markets'. Its designs are NVIDIA-certified for Blackwell: 'data halls with capacities of up to 50MW, developing individual AI clusters of up to 250MW'. The UAE pipeline includes Ajman QAJ1 (100 MW IT in 20 halls of 5 MW, liquid-cooled, initial phase due December 2026), AUH4 at Mafraq and AUH8 at Masdar City (60 MW combined), and Microsoft's 200 MW Azure expansion from the end of 2026. Abroad: Dammam (land of 225,000 m² for up to 200 MW), Lombardy with Eni (500 MW IT, heads of terms; the European Commission cleared the joint venture in August 2026) and Ankara (up to 100 MW). Tenants include e& ('a major tenant'), Microsoft and the Stargate UAE operators.
highlights: Financing: 'a $2.62 billion financing facility … with two top UAE banks – Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (ADCB) and First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB). With a tenor lasting up to 10 years' (Sep 2025)
Build model: 'modular design and construction strategy'; 'adiabatic free cooling and liquid-to-liquid cooling solutions'; AUH6 has '7MW of energy that's solar generated'
22 of 30 UAE facilities hold Uptime Tier III Constructed Facility certification (Feb 2026); in-house operations through Khazna NexOps (230+ staff, Feb 2026)
Power: Ajman QAJ1's grid supply is 'primarily provided by Etihad Water and Electricity Company (EtihadWE)'; Lombardy would draw on an Eni combined-cycle plant designed with CO2 capture
productsAndServices.positioning: The UAE's dominant wholesale operator (73% share, company); a regional challenger abroad, entering Saudi Arabia, Italy and Türkiye against incumbent landlords
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct long-term wholesale leases and build-to-suit for hyperscalers, telcos and AI operators; general contractors appointed per site
targetSegments: AI labs and their operators (OpenAI, Oracle)
productsAndServices.roadmap: More than 1 GW of new capacity within five years, over 400 MW of it international (Oct 2025); QAJ1 initial phase and AUH4 by December 2026; AUH8 August 2026; Microsoft 200 MW online from end-2026

productsAndServices.name: Stargate UAE and the 5 GW UAE–US AI Campus
productsAndServices.description: Stargate UAE is 'a 1-gigawatt compute cluster' that 'will be built by G42 and operated by OpenAI and Oracle', with Cisco on security and connectivity, SoftBank as a partner and NVIDIA supplying 'the latest NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB300 systems' (launch, 22 May 2025). It sits within the UAE–US AI Campus, a planned 5 GW, 10-square-mile hub in Abu Dhabi 'powered by nuclear, solar, and natural gas', unveiled on 15 May 2025. G42's October 2025 update: 'being developed by Khazna Data Centers', on a 'design-to-build approach'; 'Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems are also being finalized, and key modular components have entered production. The project has completed procurement of all long-lead equipment and has already received its first deliveries of mechanical systems'. Chips deploy inside G42's 'Regulated Technology Environment', approved under BIS guidelines.
highlights: First 200 MW targeted for 2026; Khaldoon Al Mubarak said it would be 'in place and ready at some point in the third quarter' of 2026 (The National, Dec 2025); no first-party confirmation of energisation by 26 Sep 2026

Reuters (11 Sep 2026): the campus 'will now likely comprise a network of data centers spread across the UAE' after Iranian attacks on Gulf data centres; G42 says the project is 'subject to continuous review'
No power, cooling or electrical supplier and no EPC contractor is named for Stargate UAE in any first-party or third-party source found
Sam Altman: 'the first major milestone in our OpenAI for Countries initiative'
productsAndServices.positioning: The flagship of the US–UAE AI Acceleration Partnership; physically and politically the anchor of G42's export-control arrangements
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Built by Khazna for operation by OpenAI and Oracle
targetSegments: US and UAE hyperscale tenants of the wider 5 GW campus
productsAndServices.roadmap: First 200 MW in 2026; the full 1 GW over about three years (Khazna CEO, The National, Oct 2025); campus siting under revision (Reuters, Sep 2026)

productsAndServices.name: Core42 — sovereign cloud and AI compute
productsAndServices.category: GPU cloud / neocloud and sovereign cloud
productsAndServices.description: Core42 (Core42 Technology Projects LLC), founded by G42 in 2023, is 'the core of G42's Intelligence Grid, building and operating the systems that turn power and silicon into tokens'. Products: a Sovereign AI Cloud ('Harness the power of NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Microsoft, or Cerebras'; 'Access 86K+ GPUs across sovereign data centers globally'), with self-service H100 capacity launched at GITEX in October 2025 under a 'tiered vetting system aligned with license conditions'. Also a Sovereign Public Cloud on Microsoft Azure regional infrastructure with the Core42 Insight control layer, a Signature Private Cloud for secret and top-secret workloads, and the Compass model gateway. Its capacity is mostly leased: 60 MW of critical IT at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner, New York, where the Maximus-01 cluster of 'more than 9,000 AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs' ranked 20th on the TOP500. Other sites include Dallas, Sunnyvale, Stockton and Minneapolis (the Condor Galaxy systems with Cerebras), Grenoble with DataOne, an Italian cluster with Domyn, and a framework for up to 10,000 GPUs from Northern Data's Taiga Cloud.
highlights: '10 operational sites globally and additional deployments planned for 2026' (June 2026)
Financing: 'two structured trade finance facilities … amounting to USD550 million with HSBC', non-dilutive (Feb and May 2026)

SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 3.0 (23 Sep 2026): Participation Ribbon — 'a dark horse … solid team, allocation of GPUs, political backing'; ClusterMAX 2.1 noted compliance restrictions preventing testing, or renting by anyone outside the UAE, at the UAE sites
productsAndServices.positioning: A sovereign-first neocloud: licence-compliant access and government-grade controls rather than price; rated below the medallion tiers by SemiAnalysis
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to UAE government and enterprise; self-service cloud; e& UAE 'Sovereign AI Compute' channel (Jul 2026); Mubadala's Solutions+ for Oracle services
targetSegments: UAE government and Abu Dhabi entities
AI labs and developers (US and Europe)
productsAndServices.roadmap: European headquarters in Dublin operating from early 2026; the 108 MW expansion option at Lake Mariner not shown exercised

productsAndServices.name: Sovereign-AI programmes and models abroad
productsAndServices.description: G42 exports the sovereign-AI model through G42 International, whose chief executive's mandate includes 'the UAE–US 5GW AI Campus and Stargate UAE'. Programmes: Condor Galaxy India, an '8-exaflop AI supercomputing cluster comprising 64 Cerebras CS-3 systems' (commercial terms May 2026); a Vietnam framework with FPT and Viet Thai Group 'backed by consumption commitments of up to $1 billion' across three data-centre locations (framework only); 'Digital Embassies' and the Greenshield control layer (Jan 2026); a Kenya geothermal-powered data-centre plan with Microsoft (2024). Models come from Inception and MBZUAI: Jais (Arabic), NANDA (Hindi-English) and K2 Think.
highlights: Assurance Compute Framework (Feb 2026): 'intent to develop' geolocation verification and cryptographic tracking of US-origin chips inside the Regulated Technology Environment
productsAndServices.positioning: G42 sells sovereignty as a service to governments that cannot build it themselves
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vietnam site development after the framework; Condor Galaxy India installation by G42 with C-DAC

productsAndServices.name: Other operating companies — Presight, Space42, M42, CPX
productsAndServices.description: G42's group also holds Presight (big-data analytics, ADX-listed; Q1 2026 revenue AED 689.0M, +22.2%), Space42 (satellites, ADX-listed), M42 (health, with Mubadala), CPX (cyber security, acquired October 2024), AIQ (the Presight–ADNOC joint venture) and Astratech. G42 sold about 2% of Presight through an accelerated bookbuild in September 2025.
highlights: None of these units is an equipment buyer for data-centre power on the record

relationships.scale: US$1.5B minority stake; a board seat
relationships.via: Azure (Core42 Sovereign Public Cloud); 200 MW expansion delivered through Khazna
relationships.note: Microsoft invested US$1.5B in G42 for a minority stake in April 2024, Brad Smith joined the G42 board, and the work is governed by an Intergovernmental Assurance Agreement.
relationships.context:
The April 2024 announcement also moved G42's AI applications onto Microsoft Azure and created a US$1B developer fund. The percentage has never been disclosed.

Microsoft is also Khazna's tenant: the November 2025 release announced a 200 MW Azure expansion 'delivered through Khazna Data Centers', to start coming online before the end of 2026. Microsoft's own November 2025 account of its UAE programme counts the US$1.5B as part of US$15.2B of UAE spending from 2023 to 2029.

relationships.note: MGX holds an undisclosed minority stake in Khazna alongside Silver Lake, bought as e& exited in March 2025; G42 was one of MGX's two foundational partners at its creation in 2024.
relationships.context:
Khazna's March 2025 release welcomed 'MGX and Silver Lake as new minority shareholders, alongside majority shareholder G42'. e& sold its 40% for US$2.2B under a binding agreement with G42 and Khazna of 25 Feb 2025.

The two share a chairman: Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed chairs both G42 and MGX. MGX's board has described the Khazna stake as its route into Stargate UAE.

relationships.scale: Stargate UAE: 1 GW cluster; first 200 MW in 2026
relationships.note: Stargate UAE, a 1 GW cluster, 'will be built by G42 and operated by OpenAI and Oracle' — the first project of OpenAI's 'OpenAI for Countries' initiative.
relationships.context: Announced 22 May 2025 with Oracle, NVIDIA, Cisco and SoftBank. G42's November 2025 wording is 'being built by G42 for OpenAI in partnership with Oracle, Cisco, NVIDIA, and SoftBank Group'. Khazna is the developer. Commercial terms between G42 and OpenAI are not disclosed. OpenAI told Reuters in September 2026 it was making 'good progress on the infrastructure and adoption priorities needed to deliver it'.

relationships.note: Oracle co-operates Stargate UAE with OpenAI on the cluster G42 builds.
relationships.context: The launch release names Oracle as operator with OpenAI. No Oracle-side release or contract terms for Stargate UAE were found.

relationships.note: NVIDIA supplies the GB300 systems for Stargate UAE and has certified Khazna's data-hall designs for Blackwell.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's own Q1 FY2026 results release lists Stargate UAE with 'strategic partners G42, OpenAI, Oracle, SoftBank Group and Cisco'. In June 2025 NVIDIA certified Khazna's next-generation designs for Blackwell (halls up to 50 MW, clusters up to 250 MW). US approvals allowed G42 up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips in November 2025, and licence-free access from July 2026.

relationships.scale: 60 MW critical IT (72.5 MW gross); about US$1.1B over ten years
relationships.via: turn-key data-centre leases at Lake Mariner, New York
relationships.note: TeraWulf is Core42's US landlord: 60 MW of critical IT at Lake Mariner on 10-year leases backed by a G42 parent guarantee.
relationships.context: TeraWulf announced 'over 70 MW' gross in December 2024 (2 + 16 + 42 MW critical IT). Its 8-K call transcript gives $125 per kW-month with a 3% escalator and a 12-month revenue prepayment. All 60 MW was operational by 31 Mar 2026. An option for a further 108 MW of critical IT is not shown exercised, and TeraWulf's Q2 2026 release does not mention Core42.

relationships.via: AMD Instinct MI300X (Maximus-01); MI350X cluster with Cisco
relationships.note: AMD supplies the GPUs in Core42's Maximus-01 cluster at Lake Mariner — more than 9,000 MI300X, ranked 20th on the TOP500.
relationships.context: G42's November 2025 release reports Maximus-01's TOP500 ranking (114.50 PF Rmax). A Cisco-integrated AMD MI350X cluster in the UAE was announced in October 2025, 'pending final approvals'. G42 and AMD also partnered on AI compute in France (Grenoble with DataOne, 2025).

relationships.note: HUMAIN is the Gulf's other sovereign AI builder; the US approved both for up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips on the same day, and since July 2026 only G42 holds licence-free access.
relationships.context: US Commerce's 19 Nov 2025 statement covered 'G42 … and Humain' together. The July 2026 BIS rule moved the UAE, not Saudi Arabia, to Country Group A:5. Khazna's entry into Dammam (up to 200 MW, December 2025) puts G42's landlord in HUMAIN's home market.

policyExposure.exposure: BIS moved the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 to A:5. It listed 'Group 42 Holding Ltd d/b/a/G42, including G42 Cloud Technology LLC' and 'Core42 Technology Projects LLC d/b/a/ Core42' as approved recipients of advanced computing items in Supplement No. 8 to Part 740 — not for the wider STA licence exception. The approval 'shall automatically expire on April 6, 2027' unless 'the two UAE-based AI companies … become U.S. companies', and it 'does not overcome the end-use and end-user based license requirements in part 744'. Before this rule G42 held a November 2025 approval for up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips.
policyExposure.mitigation: Deployment inside G42's 'Regulated Technology Environment … approved under U.S. Department of Commerce and Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) guidelines'; the Assurance Compute Framework (Feb 2026). G42's statement welcoming the rule does not mention the April 2027 condition.

policyExposure.exposure: G42's Microsoft partnership 'is governed by a detailed Intergovernmental Assurance Agreement between G42 and Microsoft', developed with the UAE and US governments. G42 says that as corporate policy it and its affiliates 'do not conduct business with any entity listed on the U.S. Government Consolidated Screening List', with a Microsoft–G42 compliance committee meeting quarterly (Sep 2024).

policyExposure.regime: US congressional scrutiny of China ties
policyExposure.exposure: Members of Congress have pressed repeatedly on G42's China links: a January 2024 Select Committee letter, a July 2024 request by the House Foreign Affairs and China Select Committee chairs for an intelligence-community assessment, and Senator Warren's July 2026 statement on the A:5 decision. The FT's October 2025 report of US intelligence findings is denied by G42 as 'false and defamatory'.
policyExposure.mitigation: G42 (Jan 2024): 'we have pursued a commercial strategy since 2022 to fully align with our U.S. partners and not to engage with Chinese companies'

policyExposure.exposure: The European Commission found the Eni–Khazna Lombardy joint venture 'would not raise competition concerns, given the limited combined market positions'; the stake split is undisclosed and the project remains at heads-of-terms stage.

financials.commentary: The financial record is the counterparties' — e&'s exchange filing on Khazna, TeraWulf's on Core42 — plus Khazna's and Core42's own financing releases and the listed Presight. Collection gap: group revenue, Khazna's revenue and EBITDA, capex on Stargate UAE, and the ownership percentages of G42, MGX, Silver Lake and Microsoft.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Khazna, not G42 group or Core42, is the entity that buys power equipment, and that Stargate UAE's first 200 MW is already bought. Basis: e&'s filing — 'Khazna designs, builds and operates wholesale data centers'. G42's October 2025 update: Stargate UAE is 'being developed by Khazna' on a 'design-to-build approach' and 'has completed procurement of all long-lead equipment'. Khazna carries its own debt (US$2.62B), buys its own land and appoints its own contractors (Laing O'Rourke at Ajman), while Core42 leases shells (TeraWulf) and buys IT. The first 200 MW's suppliers are undisclosed, so the open door is the next 800 MW and the rest of Khazna's more-than-1 GW pipeline. Indicator to watch: a named EPC or electrical supplier for Stargate UAE's later phases, or for the dispersed campus sites Reuters describes.

(High confidence) We assess that the 6 April 2027 sunset in the BIS approval is the single fact most likely to change G42's structure in the next six months. Basis: the rule text makes G42's and Core42's licence-free status expire unless they 'become U.S. companies'. Bloomberg reports talks on a majority sale to US companies or a US vehicle (4 Sep 2026), and on raising billions (2 Sep 2026). G42's own statement on the rule omits the condition. Indicator to watch: a US-domiciled G42 or Core42 entity, a named US acquirer, or a BIS notice extending the date.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Khazna has an 800 VDC conversation under way, making it the one Gulf landlord on the record with a DC-architecture opening. Basis: the Siemens memorandum (15 Sep 2026) says 'The companies will continue to progress next-generation 800 VDC power architectures and their potential in AI data centers'. 'Continue' implies earlier work. Khazna's designs carry NVIDIA's Blackwell certification and 'future-proofing for Rubin as standard'. The memorandum is not an award, and no SST, HVDC or battery supplier is named. Indicator to watch: an 800 VDC pilot hall or a Siemens award at a Khazna site.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Stargate UAE's power and physical design is back in flux. Basis: Reuters (11 Sep 2026, six people familiar) reports the 5 GW campus will likely become a network of sites across the UAE, with air defences and possibly underground construction, after Iranian drones struck AWS data centres in the UAE and Bahrain on 1 Mar 2026. The campus's utility counterparty is not named first-party; only 'nuclear, solar, and natural gas' is. Khaldoon Al Mubarak's third-quarter 2026 date for the first 200 MW is unconfirmed. Indicator to watch: an energisation announcement for the first 200 MW, or a new site list.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the China-ties question is a standing risk to every US decision G42 depends on, not a closed file. Basis: congressional letters in 2024 and 2026 and the FT's October 2025 report of US intelligence findings, which G42 calls 'false and defamatory'. Senator Warren's statement ties the A:5 decision to a Tahnoon-linked investment in a Trump-family crypto company. Indicator to watch: any BIS action under Part 744 end-user rules, or Commerce testimony on the UAE decision.
